## Interactive R with Shiny

```{r setup, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#Load packages
library(tidyverse);library(here);library(lubridate)

#Load data
nutrient_data <- read.csv(
  here('Data','raw','NTL-LTER_Lake_Nutrients_PeterPaul_Processed.csv'),
  stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

#Fix dates
nutrient_data$sampledate = ymd(nutrient_data$sampledate)

#Set a default plotting theme
my_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray", linewidth = 0.5),
      panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "lightgray", linewidth = 0.25),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)
    )

theme_set(my_theme)

```


```{r Plot Functions, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Create plotting function
plot_it <- function(the_parameter,start_year,end_year){
  #Plot the values given
  nutrient_data %>% 
    filter(year4 > start_year & year4 < end_year) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(
      x = sampledate,
      #y = .data[[the_parameter]], #-or-
      y = !!sym(the_parameter),
      color = depth,
      shape = lakename)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 2) +
    scale_x_date(
      date_breaks = "1 years",
      date_labels = '%Y') +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(17, 18)) +
    labs(
      title = "Concentration over time, by depth and lake",
      x = "Date", 
      y = expression(Concentration ~ (mu*g / L)), 
      shape = "Lake", 
      color = "Depth (m)") +
    scale_color_viridis_c(
      option = "mako", 
      guide = guide_colorbar(reverse = T),
      direction = -1)
}

```


```{r widget exploration, echo=FALSE}
# Create a selectInput widget to select which nutrient to display in the plot
selectInput(
  inputId =  "the_parameter",
  label = "Select the nutrient to show",
  choices = c('tn_ug','tp_ug','nh34','no23','po4'),
  selected = 'tn_ug'
)

# Create a sliderInput to set the date range
sliderInput(
  inputId = 'yearSlider',
  label = 'Select a date range',
  min = min(nutrient_data$year4),
  max = max(nutrient_data$year4),
  step = 1,
  round=T,
  sep='',
  value = c(min(nutrient_data$year4),max(nutrient_data$year4))
)

# Create a renderPlot object to display the plot 
# created with the plot_it function
renderPlot(
  plot_it(
    input$the_parameter,
    input$yearSlider[1],
    input$yearSlider[2]
    )
)
```
